subject: Usage-led commit amendment - Medicore Dedicated GPUs
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Holmes <kate.holmes@medicore.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Usage-led commit amendment - Medicore Dedicated GPUs

Hi Kate,

Thanks again for the time last week. We completed the utilization analysis for your dedicated fleet and wanted to propose a short amendment to your current commitment that aligns to the sustained usage we've observed. Key findings: 

- Observed sustained GPU utilization: 88–94% (weighted across p50/p95 windows) for the past 60 days; peak periodic bursts to 98% during clinic syncs.
- Prefetch/caching reduces per-request latency at p50, but p95 token latency increases when utilization is above ~90% on the current 24-GPU tranche.
- Forecasted Q1 demand (based on onboarding schedule and new inference pipelines) shows a 22% incremental token volume vs. current committed capacity.

Proposal (summary):
- Add 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs to your Dedicated tranche with immediate activation (billed under an amendment that reprofiles 12 months of the existing commit).
- Reprofile schedule: shift 3 months of the remaining tranche from Q3 into Q1 and add the 4 GPU tranche now to address latency and avoid throttling/fallbacks.
- Net monthly delta: approx +$12,400 (detailed in attached TCO).

Attachments: medicore_utilization_report_q4_2025.pdf, amended_commit_schedule_MED-2025-047.xlsx

Ask: Can we align on the amendment by EOD Friday so we can provision the capacity before your Q1 onboarding? Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk the math.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime

From: Kate Holmes <kate.holmes@medicore.ai>

Cc: procurement@medicore.ai
Date: 2026-01-13T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage-led commit amendment - Medicore Dedicated GPUs

Marcus,

Appreciate the analysis and the quick turnaround. A couple of questions before procurement will sign off:

1) Can you show the expected improvement in p95 latency (ms) for our critical /patient-lookup route with the +4 GPUs? We need a clear SLA uplift to justify the incremental spend.
2) Is there a phased option (2 GPUs now, 2 GPUs in 6 weeks) — procurement prefers smoothing capex within this quarter where possible.
3) Any alternatives that keep us within our current cash flow runway (e.g., temporary burst pool + autoscaling vs committed GPUs)?

Also, procurement asked for a one-page justification they can attach to the PO. Can you provide that?

Kate Holmes
Head of ML Platform | Medicore Health
kate.holmes@medicore.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Holmes <kate.holmes@medicore.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Usage-led commit amendment - Medicore Dedicated GPUs

Hi Kate — thanks for the follow-ups. Quick answers and appended math below.

1) p95 latency impact: Our simulation (attached tco_delta_calculation_MED-2025-047.csv) estimates p95 token latency for /patient-lookup drops from ~420ms to ~265ms with the additional 4 GPUs under your observed request profile (steady-state plus clinic-day bursts). That's a 37% reduction at p95 and reduces the observed tail that has triggered fallbacks twice last month.

2) Phased option: Yes — we can do 2 GPUs now and 2 GPUs in 6 weeks. Pricing model options: (a) immediate 4 GPUs under amendment (lower monthly unit charge) or (b) staged add with a small staging premium (~6% on staged tranche) because of the operational churn. We included both options in amended_commit_schedule_MED-2025-047.xlsx.

3) Alternatives: Temporary burst pool with autoscale can absorb spikes but will not materially change sustained p95 latency; it's a cheaper short-term mitigation but adds unpredictability to cost and occasionally leads to cold-starts for very large batches. If you want, procurement can approve a modest burst budget for Q1 while we stage the committed tranche.

Attached: tco_delta_calculation_MED-2025-047.csv and the amended_commit_schedule spreadsheet.

One-page justification (copy below — you can paste into the PO attachment):

---
Medicore Dedicated Commitment Amendment — Executive Summary
- Business need: Sustained GPU utilization >88% causing p95 latency degradation and intermittent fallbacks, impacting clinician workflows during peak syncs.
- Proposed change: Add 4 GPUs to the existing Dedicated tranche and reprofile remaining commit to accelerate delivery into Q1. Option to stage 2 + 2 exists.
- Expected impact: ~37% reduction in p95 latency for /patient-lookup route; expected avoidance of fallback-induced error rate spikes (~0.8% reduction in user-visible errors).
- Cost delta: +$12,400/month (immediate 4 GPU amendment) or phased option with small staging premium.
- Ask: Procurement approval for amendment MED-2025-047 by EOD Jan 20 to guarantee provisioning window prior to Q1 onboarding.
---

Let me know which pricing option procurement prefers and I'll get an amendment and DocuSign link over today/tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus
